summary: POC scoping call to agree success criteria, workload sizing, and shortlist open models for Endeavor Health's clinical summarization use case. Discussed multilingual needs (EN/ES), latency targets, data residency and VPC options. Agreed next steps for benchmarks and pilot SOW.
transcript:
[00:00] Samir Patel: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Samir from Redwood, AE on the account, and with me is Lena from SE. How's everyone?
[00:10] Maya Chen: Hi Samir, thanks, Maya here. Big thanks. We pulled in Ravi and Olivia. We're excited to scope the POC.
[00:18] Ravi Singh: Morning. Quick note, we care a lot about latency and PHI handling — this is clinical notes summarization.
[00:25] Lena Ortiz: Got it, thanks Ravi. We'll walk through success criteria then sizing then model shortlist.
[00:34] Samir Patel: High level — what's a successful POC for you? Maya?
[00:40] Maya Chen: Success for us is three things: first, summaries with >85% clinical fidelity vs our MD labels, second latency under 700ms p95 for single-document summarization, and third integration into our pipeline with no PHI leaving our VPC during pilot. Also multilingual support for Spanish ~10% of traffic.
[01:05] Lena Ortiz: Helpful. For the PHI / VPC note, Redwood Private supports a VPC deployment and we can run the pilot in your VPC or on our dedicated private tenancy. We noted dedicated GPU pools if you want predictable throughput.
[01:22] Olivia Park: For compliance we need SOC2 evidence, KMS integration, audit logs — you'll send those docs right?
[01:30] Samir Patel: Yes, we'll attach a SOC2 summary and our compliance pack after the call.
[01:36] Ravi Singh: Workload size — current production is about 1.2M notes/month, avg doc length ~1.8k tokens, spike to 3k tokens. POC can be a 100k note sample, but we need representative distribution across length and Spanish mix.
[01:55] Lena Ortiz: Great. For sizing that implies we need to evaluate throughput and memory — long sequences push KV cache and memory. For example Llama-2 70B quantized needs X GB KV per shard, smaller models cheaper.
[02:11] Samir Patel: Our typical tradeoff conversation: quality vs cost vs latency. For open models we usually shortlist a 3-model stack: a smaller fast 7–13B, a mid 13–33B, and a larger 65–70B. We'll propose specific models.
[02:27] Maya Chen: Which specific open models do you recommend for clinical summarization and spanish?
[02:32] Lena Ortiz: For POC we often suggest Mistral-Instruct / Mistral 7B-Instruct or Mistral-8x as small/mid, Llama-2-Chat 13B or 70B (or Llama3 equivalents) as mid/large, and mix in specialized medically-tuned models like MedAlpaca variants or BloomZ for multilingual. Replicate/Meta forks and RedPajama derivatives also show up.
[02:55] Ravi Singh: Any concerns about hallucination in 13B vs 70B?
[03:00] Lena Ortiz: Yes, hallucination usually decreases with model size and instruction tuning, but you can mitigate with prompts, retrieval-augmented generation, and more conservative decoding. For clinical fidelity we recommend a human-in-the-loop validation step and a scoring eval set.
[03:17] Maya Chen: Benchmarks — what metrics will you run?
[03:20] Lena Ortiz: We'll run ROUGE/L, BERTScore for similarity, and clinical entity F1 against your gold labels. Also latency p50/p95, tokens/sec throughput, GPU memory per shard, and cost per 1k tokens. We'll include a hallucination rate metric via human spot checks.
[03:39] Samir Patel: Timeline — can we run an initial bench within 2 weeks once you provide the sample prompts and 5k notes?
[03:46] Maya Chen: Two weeks ok. We need the SOW and pricing to circulate to procurement first.
[03:51] Samir Patel: We'll aim to send SOW/pricing in 48 hours.
[03:54] Ravi Singh: About model quantization — will Redwood support int8/int4 to reduce cost?
[03:58] Lena Ortiz: Yes, our runtime supports 8-bit and 4-bit quantization for many model families, but performance/quality tradeoffs vary. For example int4 on a 70B can reduce memory but might slightly affect prosaic reasoning; we'll include recommended quant profiles in the benchmark config.
[04:16] Maya Chen: Data residency — can logs or telemetry be disabled? We need to ensure no PHI telemetry leaves.
[04:22] Samir Patel: For Private deployments, telemetry can be limited; audit logs can be kept in your KMS-backed storage. We'll detail that in the compliance pack.
[04:30] Maya Chen: For Spanish, do you have recommended models that are strong multilingual and clinical?
[04:35] Lena Ortiz: BLOOMZ variants and XGen multilingual ones have decent Spanish. Also Llama-3-chat shows strong multi-lingual behavior. If high-quality Spanish clinical summarization is critical, consider fine-tuning a 13B on a small in-domain corpus — low-cost compared to fine-tuning 70B.
[04:53] Ravi Singh: Ok noted. Benchmarks: we want to see p95 latency on our infra, cost per summary, and entity recall.
[05:01] Lena Ortiz: We'll provide a benchmark plan: sample harness (how we call the API, batching strategy, sequence lengths), hardware matrix (dedicated GPU types we recommend), and model variants including quantization and small fine-tuned checkpoints.
[05:16] Maya Chen: Who will run the bench? Redwood or our infra?
[05:19] Samir Patel: Prefer Redwood runs on our dedicated pilot environment in your VPC — that way we can isolate data and measure realistic lat/throughput. Alternatively we can run portable tests on similar-sized infra and share reproducible scripts.
[05:32] Olivia Park: On legal, we need a data processing addendum, plus a checklist for customer-managed keys.
[05:38] Samir Patel: We'll include DPA template and KMS integration notes.
[05:41] Ravi Singh: Anything else on success criteria? We'll add acceptance thresholds: clinical F1 > 0.82 and hallucination < 3% on spot checks.
[05:50] Maya Chen: Yes let's add that. Also acceptance triggered when integration results in end-to-end latency under 800ms and cost below $0.10 per summary for the pilot volume.
[06:02] Lena Ortiz: Noted. For model shortlist I'll send a proposed table: Model | Expected quality | expected latency | cost ballpark | multilingual score. Does that work?
[06:12] Maya Chen: Perfect.
[06:14] Samir Patel: Recap and next steps: Samir send SOW + pricing by Thursday, Lena send benchmark config + model shortlist and quant profiles by Friday, Maya provide 5k sample notes and acceptance thresholds by Monday. Then we'll schedule the pilot bench wk of 11/15.
[06:31] Maya Chen: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[06:33] Samir Patel: Thanks all. We'll follow up in email with links to docs and SOC2.
[06:38] [call ends]
